title: ElevenLabs doubles to a $22 billion valuation on voice-agent demand
subtitle: A $300 million employee tender offer led by Wellington and T. Rowe Price values the AI voice startup at twice its February round, as its agents reach 15 million conversations per week.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: ElevenLabs completed a $300 million employee tender offer on September 30, valuing the AI voice-generation company at $22 billion — twice the valuation it secured in a February 2026 funding round. The transaction was led by Wellington and T. Rowe Price, with EQT, Goldman Sachs, GIC, Ontario Teachers' Pension Plan, Sapphire Ventures, and BDT & MSD investing for the first time. Enterprise now accounts for 55% of ElevenLabs' revenue, with Stripe, Deutsche Telekom, and DoorDash-owned SevenRooms among the firms that have deployed ElevenAgents. The company's voice agents are handling more than 15 million conversations per week — three times the February level. Founded in 2022 and headquartered in New York and London, ElevenLabs now sits among Europe's most valuable private startups.

A tender offer doubling a company's valuation inside eight months tells you where private capital thinks the voice-agent category is going. The underlying number — 15 million conversations per week, up 3x since February — is what justifies the markup. That is not voice-cloning demand; voice cloning is a feature that was commodified in 2024. The driver is agent-to-caller volume: outbound sales, inbound support, scheduling, telephony routing, each replacing a human seat on a call. Stripe and Deutsche Telekom are the signal — enterprise buyers with regulatory exposure signing production contracts, not pilots.

The deal lands alongside Google's Gemini 4 Argon launch and the FTC's new safety probe, both the same day. The three stories together describe the market's current posture: capability races at the frontier, regulatory pressure on the labs that run them, and a voice-agent layer growing fast enough that incumbent telecom and payments firms are routing calls through it. ElevenLabs has avoided the frontier-model race entirely and sold shovels to companies that use frontier models — a strategy also visible in Scale, Together, and Modal's recent raises.

For learners: when a company's valuation moves faster than its revenue, the market is pricing a specific bet. In ElevenLabs' case, the bet is that most phone-shaped interactions in the enterprise will be handled by an AI agent within three years, and that voice is a defensible layer under whichever LLM wins. If you are evaluating a career move or a product opportunity, voice agents and the tooling around them (telephony, routing, transcript analytics, consent capture) are a less contested surface than text chat right now, and the regulatory requirements — recording consent, disclosure, auditability — are already clearer.
